No-hands slab. On a slab, hands off — see how high you climb on feet alone. Weight through the toes and trust the rubber. Go.
Nose to the wall. Before each reach, bring your nose toward the next hold — get hips and chest into the wall before you pull. Move your body, not just your arm. Go.
Off. Down. Breathe. Chalk up for the next one.
One foot off. Climb using only one foot; the other flags to balance. Swap feet between attempts. Builds tension and trust on the working foot. Go.
One-hand climbing. Climb an easy problem using only one hand — the other hovers off. Switch hands each go. Forces precise feet and body position. Go.
Open-hand only. Climb easy problems using only open-hand grips — no crimping. Builds resilient fingers and trust in friction. Go.
Power-endurance burn. Find a pumpy circuit or traverse: 45s on / climb continuously, step off before failure. Go.
Precision touch. Reach for the next hold and freeze a beat right before you touch it, then land it exactly. No regrips, no readjusting. Go.
Pulse raiser. Get the blood moving — easy bike, brisk walk, or stairs, plus shoulder circles, wrist prep and hip openers.
Quiet downclimbing. Downclimb easy problems under control. Doubles your footwork mileage and builds stamina. Go.
Quiet downclimbing. Downclimb easy problems with control. Builds footwork, body awareness and stamina at the same time. Go.
